title: Batch triage rubric for Sales/CS enterprise feature bundles
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Sales and CS often send high-volume, loosely related enterprise feature requests as individual asks. That creates backlog noise, inconsistent scope estimates, and duplicated follow-up work. Goal: introduce a lightweight batch triage rubric that lets PMs and Solutions Engineers aggregate related requests into 'feature bundles', provide an initial priority score, a 1-2 sentence scoped summary, recommended rollout path (hosted / dedicated / private), and a rough engineering estimate. Deliverables: (1) a one-page rubric template for Sales/CS to use during intake, (2) an internal PM scoring sheet and automation to group similar asks, (3) a pilot process + 4-week rollout plan with feedback loops to Sales and CS.
acceptance_criteria: Rubric template published to Confluence and shared with Sales/CS
Automated grouping rule implemented (similarity threshold) in intake dashboard demo
Five pilot bundles triaged with documented scores and preliminary estimates
Handoff checklist created for Eng/Design with required artifacts (mock, success metric, security flags)
Sales and CS report >50% reduction in duplicate triage follow-ups during pilot
updates: 2025-11-15: Discovery workshop with Sales leadership (Alyssa R., Mateo V.) — observed 3 common request patterns: security/SLA asks, capacity/scaling requests, and feature parity asks.
2025-12-02: Prototyped rubric fields: business impact, user count, compliance/regulatory requirement, rollout complexity, preferred timeline, and estimated engineering points.
2026-01-10: Engineering sync — ENG flagged need for a stability/security indicator and requested explicit acceptance criteria per bundle. ENG suggested default estimate buckets (1, 3, 8, 20).
2026-02-02: Pilot plan approved by PM leadership. Selected 6 candidate requests from Sales (North America enterprise accounts) to form 3 bundles.
2026-03-05: Ran first pilot triage; two bundles required deeper product discovery — created follow-up research tasks.
2026-03-13: Incorporated pilot feedback: added 'compatibility with Dedicated/Private' field and tightened automation similarity threshold. Preparing rollout comms to Sales.
decision_log: Use bundle-level scoring instead of re-scoring individual asks to reduce churn (PM decision 2025-12-02)
Default engineering estimate buckets adopted (1/3/8/20) to standardize quick scoping (Eng review 2026-01-10)
Priority weightings: security/regulatory x2, customer revenue x1.5, usage footprint x1.2 (Consensus 2026-01-20)
risks: Over-bundling unrelated asks could hide critical single-customer needs
Sales adoption friction if rubric is perceived as extra paperwork
Automation grouping may miss semantic nuance for regulatory asks
Engineering estimates may be optimistic without minimal viable spec
comments: Riley Morgan (Design): Can we add a quick UI sketch for the rubric card in the Console so Sales can see the resulting bundle?
Nikhil Rao (Solutions Eng): Need explicit fields for customer data residency and KMS requirements — otherwise Private deploys get miscategorized.
Maya Thompson (Sales): Proposed a lightweight two-click workflow inside our CRM to surface bundle candidates back to PMs.
Jordan Patel (PM, assignee): Will draft the Confluence template and coordinate the pilot schedule. Blocking on ENG-8421 for automation prototype.
next_steps: Finalize Confluence rubric and share with Sales/CS by 2026-03-18
Engineering to deliver a demo of the grouping automation by 2026-03-25 (ENG-8421)
Run second pilot with EMEA accounts and capture metrics (duplicate follow-ups, time-to-scope) — window 2026-03-28 to 2026-04-11
